key_insight: A microfabricated reactive multilayer platform enables localized on-chip annealing up to 1400°C for rapid materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: Localized, ultrafast thermal processing could accelerate screening of nanomaterials and access nonequilibrium structures and phases.
method: Use a buried reactive multilayer as a localized heat source.
Combine it with a nanometric diffusion barrier.
Apply rapid heating and quenching to probe solidification, phase stabilization, and melt dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports heating and quenching rates on the order of 10^6°C/s, ultra-high-aspect-ratio microstructures, dopant-free tetragonal zirconia retained at room temperature, and transient stages of capillary-driven hole collapse in melts.
watch_item: Thermal uniformity, process reproducibility, and compatibility across material systems require validation beyond the demonstrations described in the abstract.
paper_title: Reaction-induced Localized Annealing for On-chip Materials Discovery
